summary: Reviewed 3 modified files (src-tauri/src/setup.rs, src-tauri/src/lib.rs, src-tauri/Cargo.toml) plus process.rs for context. 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium (noted), 2 Low (noted), 1 Info (noted). All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM | A08 — Software & Data Integrity Failures | setup.rs: download_file() | Downloaded PHP ZIP (windows.php.net/downloads/releases/php-8.4.8-nts-Win32-vs17-x64.zip) and monitor ZIP (GitHub release asset) are not verified with a cryptographic hash or signature after download. The code relies solely on HTTPS/TLS transport integrity. If the source server or CDN is compromised (supply chain attack), a malicious binary could be silently extracted and subsequently executed via start_tool/query_save_data. Remediation: After each download, validate the file hash against a known-good checksum published in a separate signed manifest (e.g., SHA-256 from the GitHub release JSON's 'body' or a dedicated checksums.txt asset).

MEDIUM | A01 — Broken Access Control | lib.rs: save_tool_config() | The install_path parameter is accepted from the frontend with no restriction to app-sandboxed or user-approved directories. Any existing directory writable by the app process can be targeted. The check validates only that the parent directory exists, not that it is within an expected location. While the filename is fixed to 'config.json' and the content is structured JSON (limiting impact), a compromised WebView or malicious frontend injection could overwrite config.json in sensitive locations. Remediation: Validate install_path is a canonical subdirectory of app_data_dir or an explicitly user-selected path (store user-approved path in Tauri store; compare at invocation time).

LOW | A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components | src-tauri/Cargo.toml + setup.rs: PHP_DOWNLOAD_URL constant | PHP_DOWNLOAD_URL is pinned to php-8.4.8-nts-Win32-vs17-x64.zip. Security patches to PHP require a manual constant update and a new app release. End users who install tools once and do not reinstall will remain on the pinned version indefinitely. Remediation: Derive the PHP download URL from a versioned manifest or the monitor's release metadata rather than a hardcoded constant, so updated PHP is picked up on re-install. Tracked as existing improvement note from implementation pipeline.

LOW | A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures | lib.rs: log_to_file() | The level and message parameters are written directly to the local debug.log file without stripping newline characters. A frontend caller can inject newlines to create fake log entries (log injection). Impact is low because the log is a local file used only for desktop debugging, not ingested by a SIEM or alerting system. Remediation: Strip or escape CR/LF characters from level and message before writing (e.g., replace '\n' and '\r' with a placeholder space).

INFO | A04 — Insecure Design (defence-in-depth) | setup.rs: fetch_latest_release() + download_and_install_tools() | The tag_name returned by the GitHub API is used verbatim in URL path construction (format!(..., tag)) without sanitisation. Because GITHUB_RELEASES_BASE is hardcoded to https://github.com and reqwest resolves path components within the same origin, a crafted tag_name cannot redirect to a different host. Impact is theoretical; at worst a malformed tag causes a 404. Remediation: Add a simple regex guard (e.g., r'^v?[\w.\-]+$') to reject unexpected tag formats before URL construction.

summary: Reviewed setup.rs, lib.rs, Cargo.toml, and process.rs. The new WP-002 code (setup.rs and lib.rs wrapper) is well-structured, follows Rust idioms, and satisfies all architectural requirements.

Two Fix-Forward improvements applied: (1) removed the unused #[cfg(windows)] CommandExt trait import from process.rs — tokio::process::Command exposes creation_flags as an inherent method and the trait was never used; (2) changed detect_os_arch() in setup.rs from returning an infallible Result<(String,String),String> to returning (String,String) directly — the Ok() wrapper and the ? at the call site were dead code.

One pre-existing clippy warning remains in process.rs: let _ = child.kill() in start_tool() creates an async Future that is immediately dropped (non-binding future). This predates WP-002 and requires a behavioral fix (change kill() to start_kill() to match the pattern already used in stop_tool() and stop_all()). Tagged for follow-up.

After applying Fix-Forward edits, cargo check passes cleanly. Cargo clippy now produces 1 warning (down from 2) — the remaining warning is the pre-existing kill() issue. AC-7 is conditionally met: new WP-002 code is entirely clean; the residual warning is pre-existing and tracked.

comments.note: Removed unused `#[cfg(windows)] use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;` from process.rs. `tokio::process::Command::creation_flags` is an inherent method on Windows — the std trait import was not required and generated a clippy unused-import warning.

Changed `detect_os_arch()` in setup.rs from `-> Result<(String, String), String>` to `-> (String, String)`. The function reads compile-time constants and can never fail — the Ok() wrapper and the ? propagation at the call site were dead code. Updated call site accordingly.

FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED — process.rs:38: `let _ = child.kill()` in start_tool(). `tokio::process::Child::kill()` is async; creating its Future and dropping it immediately does nothing — the old process is NOT killed when restarting a tool. This means old PHP/viewer processes accumulate in the background until app exit. Fix: change to `let _ = child.start_kill();` to match the pattern already used in stop_tool() and stop_all(). This is a behavioral change and must be applied by the Developer in a dedicated task.
